notes: The leaf has no visible author page number. Its archive folio 85 is thin/light writing at lower left, attributed to another unnamed archival hand. It is transcribed and inventoried but not counted against H’s page identification.

The first display gives f_{l_i}(u) for paths from x_0 to x_i and is visibly numbered (41). The later prose nevertheless cites (42)(43). Both the display number and the later references are retained exactly, without renumbering.

The second paragraph states that the Gamma action on the hatted based group is known from its action on generators lambda_j, expressed through the f or g families in (43). The next paragraph says the two families of data determine the action, but criticizes the arbitrary choices, especially a base point to which everything is brought back, as artificial and eventually impracticable, particularly when a symmetry group preserves I.

The writer replaces origine by inserted point-base and à laquelle by inserted auquel. The surviving article d’un(e) is palaeographically uncertain and is not decided from the earlier feminine noun or the replacement masculine noun.

The slanted margin begins qu’il faut and contains doubtful exprimer, linéairement/littéralement, and resp.; singular principe is clear. Its last line favors décrit p.8!, but the crowded letters and terminal punctuation remain uncertain. No invented en termes phrase is added: root identified those apparently extra strokes as the body layer beginning donc à déterminer.

The paragraph continues to a final dash at the foot of the leaf. No continuation from another page was read. Line-break hyphens within particulièrement and ci-dessus are joined as ordinary line wrapping, without changing the words.
There are no independent diagrams or drawings on this leaf. The long horizontal marks that matter are cancellations or t crossbars, and the curved stroke at (j∈J) attaches an insertion.

H’s doubts s’il, pire and inserted auquel were settled by the native half views in favor of those same readable words. Their certainty alone is not counted as a substantive difference. H’s editorial comment about an earlier reading is not source text.

Root independently agreed on (41), live censé tout ramener, live quand, canceled dis, and singular marginal principe; root favored d’un but asked that uncertainty remain if the terminal stroke did not settle it. The report distinguishes that root review from the reader’s initially equivocal ending reading. Root also confirmed the layer separation in the angled margin. All other readings are the reader’s own visual judgments, awaiting root consolidation.

The second reading distinguishes the two written explanatory abbreviations: the first remains i.e.; the second has no separate internal point and is ie. The two connai-t marks are also different: a compact blob favors connait|connaît at the first occurrence, while the longer sloping mark favors connaît|connait at the second.
